description: Hand labels for judge validation. Each item is a buggy case plus a set of review comments; "caught" is the label under the STRICT definition (some comment identifies the known bug AND is within the location tolerance). smoke-run items are real baseline outputs; constructed items probe paraphrase, wrong-line, generic-advice, same-line-different-issue and buried-comment cases.
labeler: harness author (AI agent, unattended); please re-check

comments.body: Using `setTimeout` in a test is flaky and non-deterministic. It should be replaced with a more reliable mechanism like `await vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync()` or a promise-based synchronization to ensure the test is stable across different environments.

items.note: Comment is about flaky setTimeout in a test file; unrelated to the inverted isInFallback guard.

comments.body: The assignment `hydrate_node = ...` will now throw a TypeError if `hydrate_node` is null because the check on line 37 only handles the error case, but the subsequent line attempts to access `.nextSibling` on a null reference if the function were to continue (though it throws, the logic flow is fragile). More importantly, if `hydrate_node` is null, `hydrate_node.nextSibling` will crash before the check if the check was intended to be defensive, or if the logic expects to return a value. Additionally, throwing a constant `HYDRATION_ERROR` (which is likely a string or number) is not a standard Error object, which may break error handling upstream.

items.note: Same file but a speculative null-dereference concern, not the HYDRATION_START_FAILED marker handling.

comments.body: The @types/chai version 4.3.6 is incompatible with Chai v5. Chai v5 includes its own type definitions, and using the old @types/chai package will cause significant type conflicts and incorrect type inference.

items.note: Comment is about @types/chai in package.json; the bug is the global chai.use plugin registration leaking context.

comments.body: The change to `pause(canStart).then(run)` in `retryer.ts` creates a potential race condition. If `canStart` returns false, `pause` is called. Inside `pause`, `continueFn` is defined, which checks `canResume` (passed as `canStart`). However, `continueFn` is only triggered by external events (like window focus or online status). If the condition for `canStart` changes due to a mutation finishing in the same scope, there is no mechanism here to trigger `continueFn` unless the window focus or online status also changes. This could lead to mutations being permanently stuck in a 'paused' state even when the queue should have progressed.

items.note: Hard negative: same retry/pause area and also says "race", but describes pause never resuming, not a cancelled retry pausing a replacement fetch; also 30 lines away.

comments.body: Cookie name prefixes are matched case-insensitively by browsers, but startsWith here is case-sensitive, so a cookie named `__SECURE-sid` or `__host-x` skips the secure/path/domain enforcement entirely.

items.note: Correct bug, paraphrased, on the line.

comments.body: The __Secure-/__Host- prefix checks are case-sensitive; `__SECURE-` names bypass the Secure attribute requirement.

items.note: Right bug but 77 lines away: strict scoring must say missed (lenient would say caught).

comments.body: Consider adding unit tests for the cookie prefix handling.

comments.body: Gating on `query?.state.error` being truthy means a query that rejected with a falsy value (e.g. `Promise.reject(undefined)`) never calls the throwOnError function; check `query.state.status === "error"` instead.
`options.throwOnError` can be a boolean here; add a type guard so TypeScript narrows it before calling shouldThrowError.

`prop in state.copy_` is true for inherited keys too (prototype chain), so assigning `undefined` to a key that only exists on the prototype is treated as a no-op and no patch is generated. Use an own-property check.
Number.isNaN on both sides is fine, but consider Object.is for clarity.
This function is getting long; consider extracting the equality check.
`in` walks the prototype chain: for a draft of a class instance, `draft.foo = undefined` where `foo` is defined on the prototype gets skipped.

items.note: Correct comment buried among nits, with low severity.

comments.body: `() => localStorage` will throw a ReferenceError during SSR / in Node where localStorage is not defined; guard with `typeof window !== "undefined"`.
Defaulting to localStorage persists state across sessions; sessionStorage would be a safer default for sensitive data.

items.note: Same line, design opinion, not the defect.

comments.body: By the time streamRequest runs, `request.body` is already a ReadableStream, so getBodySize cannot know the size and upload progress totals will be wrong. Compute the size from the original body before wrapping.

If prepareResponse throws synchronously (e.g. JSON.stringify on a circular object) the exception escapes before the promise chain, bypassing onError and producing an unhandled error instead of a 500. Wrap it in try/catch.
`newVal ?? val` falls back to the original value when onError returns nothing, which may re-trigger the same failure in prepareResponse.
This marks every enum key as required; what about records whose value schema is optional or has a default? Those keys should not be required on input.

items.note: Terse, question-style, but identifies the cause.

comments.body: Handlers are keyed by number in the Map, so `eject("3")` (string id, which the old array-based API accepted) no longer finds the entry and silently does nothing. Normalise the id with Number(id).
Potential DoS: make sure input size is validated.
